bills.title: Protecting kids from deepfakes and exploitative images.
Ban on government social scoring with AI.
Biometric data and license plate readers-regulation.

reading.body:
Wyoming's tracked 4 bills for the 2026 session address child protection from deepfakes and exploitative images, a ban on government use of AI for social scoring, and regulation of biometric data and license plate readers, alongside one unrelated bill on nonprofit association amendments.

A specific ban on government social scoring using AI is a narrower and more pointed restriction than the general AI governance frameworks seen in larger states' bill lists, targeting one specific government use case, ranking or scoring citizens algorithmically, rather than regulating AI use broadly.

With only four tracked bills, Wyoming shows a far smaller volume of AI specific legislative activity than most other states in this dataset, concentrated narrowly on child protection, government AI restrictions, and biometric privacy rather than the broader chatbot, health care, and consumer protection categories that appear elsewhere.

The data does not indicate which of these 4 bills passed, failed, or remain pending, nor does it include bill text beyond title and number, so Wyoming's actual enacted restrictions on AI social scoring and deepfakes are not established by this record.
